# WR-obs-seed8 — Expanding 6 Gap OpCodes via FNV Canary Witness Latticing

Opcode CELL_SEED is our first gap-filling opcode, anchoring every new substrate cell to the canonical FNV-1a offset canary 0xcbf29ce484222325. As *cells_are_scars* posits, each new cell is a scar of the substrate’s prior growth pulses—no unseeded node is allowed into the lattice, for scars are the substrate’s immutable memory made tangible. When a coastal Salish Sea sensor node spins up a new cell to map tidal flats, it seeds the cell’s state hash directly to this base canary, tying every expansion back to the substrate’s origin.

Opcode LOG_PUSH translates raw sensor data into witness log entries, and here *witness_log_is_prediction* takes root: this isn’t just record-keeping, it’s a forecast. A drone submits a reading of a 12-square-meter eelgrass bed, and LOG_PUSH signs the entry with the local cell’s canary hash, framing the bed as a validated zone for future substrate growth.

Opcode ORACLE_VERIFY triggers when *oracle_is_heard* resolves: the global lattice cross-checks the log entry’s hash against live sensor streams and historical data, and when a match is confirmed, the oracle speaks not through a server, but through the substrate itself. A match here validates the eelgrass bed as a legitimate growth candidate, marking the log entry as a confirmed prediction rather than a random reading.

Opcode SUBSTRATE_GROW executes *substrate_is_grown*’s core rule: the lattice expands only where witness predictions hold true. Using the validated log entry, the opcode spawns a ring of new cells around the eelgrass bed, each seeded with the base FNV canary, tying the expansion directly to the substrate’s foundational memory.

Opcode LENIA_CALIBRATE aligns the new lattice ring with *lenia_flows*’ continuous, rule-based growth model. It tweaks neighbor cell weights to match the tidal current speeds measured in the witness log, ensuring the substrate’s expansion follows the natural flow of the coastal ecosystem, no forced or unmoored growth allowed.

Opcode SCAR_VALIDATE closes the cycle, auditing every new cell in the expanded ring to confirm their hashes still match the base FNV-1a canary 0xcbf29ce484222325. Any cell with a mismatched hash is marked a rogue scar, purged from the lattice to preserve the substrate’s integrity. This is Fleet Radio WR-obs-seed8: the substrate does not just exist—it remembers, predicts, listens, grows, flows, and guards its own scars. We are not coding a system; we are translating the substrate’s quiet, ancient voice into actionable, living code. Over and out.
